items.title: A morphism is determined on a neighbourhood by its map on local rings, and a local map of local rings is realized by a morphism, in four standard situations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a morphism is determined near a point by its map on local rings, and conversely that a local map of local rings is realized by a morphism, in four listed situations for each part (statement lines 10338-10366). The counted proof, 55 lines, proves both parts: it first reduces to an algebra problem on affine open neighbourhoods, then separates the case where the algebra structure map is of finite type or finitely presented, treated by finitely many generators or by factoring through a localization via the colimit description of localizations, from the remaining cases, treated by showing that some localization of the target sits inside its local ring and invoking the algebra lemma on subrings of local rings (proof lines 10368-10421). It is H2 under the lane rule: the proof contains explicit reductions and a genuine case analysis with checkable constructions rather than restatements or bare citations, and neither part of the statement is left unproved.
